predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws the lands inside the Kingdom of Lotharingia / Holy Roman Empire shapes and, from 1260, in part inside County of Brabant and Duchy of Bavaria (eu-09-a notes: a 3.8 k km2 Hainaut piece in the 1305 Holland/Bavaria outlines).

land.text: 'Absorbed into the Burgundian Netherlands: 1432'; 'In 1432 Jacqueline had to cede the inheritance rights of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland to Duke Philip'

successors.note: From 1482 (Treaty of Arras) a province of the Habsburg Netherlands (habsburg-netherlands, this batch); the southern part (Valenciennes, Le Quesnoy, Avesnes) was ceded to France in 1659/1679 and the northern part to France in 1797 (page). Cliopatria's Duchy of Burgundy shape takes Hainaut only in 1450.

capitals.name: Mons
capitals.note: The pages name no capital. Mons is the town Humphrey of Gloucester entered in November 1424 and where he was recognised as count on 5 December 1424, and the district John IV pledged on 29 May 1418; the choice is the researcher's reading.

correction.text: the County of Hainaut: the Belgian province round Mons with Valenciennes and Avesnes in the south

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Hainaut row). The page gives no area and no boundary; the shape is the Belgian province of Hainaut (about 3,800 km2 in reality, 4,550 in the grid) with a 25 km circle at Valenciennes (3.52E 50.36N) and a 15 km circle at Avesnes (3.93E 50.12N), about 7,300 km2 in the grid, soft. The gazetteer's region 'Hainaut' (11,380 km2) is larger and probably includes the Cambrésis. The union with Flanders (1067-71 and 1191-1246) and with Holland and Zeeland (1299-1436) were personal unions and do not change the outline.

ledger.note: About 880: the county. 'The Treaty of Meerssen mentions the comitatus Hainoum, a county, and granted it to the western kingdom' (870); infobox 'Consolidation of county: ±880'. The early counts are linked to the Reginarid dynasty, whose rule before Reginar III is 'not firmly proven'.

1067: Flanders takes Hainaut. 'When the last Reginarid Count of Hainaut, Herman, the son of Reginar V, died without issue in 1051, his widow' Richilde married Baldwin VI of Flanders, and 'On the death of his father in 1067, Baldwin VI became the ruler of both Hainaut and Flanders'. Same state, new dynasty; the union lasted 1067-71 and again 1191-1246 (page).

1244: the succession war. 'The first conflict opened with Margaret's succession in 1244' (Joan died childless in 1244): John I of Avesnes, her eldest son by her first marriage, against the Dampierres of Flanders. Louis IX first assigned Hainaut to Avesnes in 1246; the page gives no dated campaign before the victory at West-Capelle on 4 July 1253.

region.text: the County of Hainaut, claimed by Avesnes and Dampierre

ledger.note: 1254: the second arbitration of Louis IX. 'The conflict closed and John I of Avesnes was secure in Hainault'; infobox 'Flanders passed to the Dampierres, Hainault to the House of Avesnes'.

1254: the House of Avesnes. Hainaut passes to the Avesnes line (John I, founder of the new line, died 1257). From 1299 Jean II 'was also Count of Holland and Zeeland' (a personal union that does not change this outline).

1356: the Bavarian-Straubing line. The page dates the union of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland under Bavaria-Straubing to 1356-1432 and says 'This branch of the Wittelsbach family held Hainaut until 1436'. The year of the Wittelsbach succession is not given as a Hainaut event.

3 July 1428: the Treaty of Delft. 'Jacqueline kept her titles of Countess of Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut', Philip of Burgundy is her heir and she may not marry without his leave; the Hainaut page: 'Already in 1428, effective control of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland was acquired by Philip the Good.'

region.text: the County of Hainaut, held for Jacqueline under Philip of Burgundy

ledger.note: 1432: 'Jacqueline had to cede the inheritance rights of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland to Duke Philip' (the Hague treaty is dated Easter 1433 on the Jacqueline page).

1432: the Burgundian Netherlands. Infobox 'Absorbed into the Burgundian Netherlands: 1432'; the succession table gives 1433; Jacqueline's rule over Hainaut is 1417-1432 in the Jacqueline succession box and her reign ends 12 April 1433 in its infobox.

wars.name: War of the Succession of Flanders and Hainault
wars.outcome: Louis IX awarded Hainaut to John I of Avesnes in 1246; Avesnes won the battle of West-Capelle on 4 July 1253 and the second arbitration of 1254 left him 'secure in Hainault'; 'Flanders passed to the Dampierres'.

wars.name: Jacqueline's war over Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland

zones.text: the County of Hainaut, with Mons

wars.outcome: Humphrey of Gloucester was recognised as count of Hainaut on 5 December 1424; John III of Bavaria died on 6 January 1425; the Treaty of Delft (3 July 1428) left Jacqueline her titles with Philip as heir.
wars.note: The Jacqueline page gives no dated account of a war between 1425 and 1428.

certainty.note: The pages give counts, treaties and towns, not boundaries; the outline is the Belgian province with two French circles.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (3 pages; budget 5). New state: Cliopatria has no Hainaut row. eu-09-a's notes (county-of-holland, county-of-brabant) asked for a county-of-hainaut dossier for at least 1260-1433.

SCOPE. 880 to 1432 (infobox 'Absorbed into the Burgundian Netherlands: 1432'). The Holland dossier (eu-09-a) ends in 1433 on the Holland page; this one follows the Hainaut infobox. After 1432 the land is part of the Burgundian and then Habsburg Netherlands (habsburg-netherlands, which includes Belgian Hainaut in its shapes). The French cessions of the south (1659 Treaty of the Pyrenees, 1679 Nijmegen: Valenciennes, Le Quesnoy, Avesnes) and the 1797 cession of the north are not dated beyond that by the page and belong to the Habsburg Netherlands and France.

SHAPES. Belgian province of Hainaut (admin1) with a 25 km circle at Valenciennes (3.52E 50.36N) and a 15 km circle at Avesnes (3.93E 50.12N). Gazetteer names wanted: 'Valenciennes', 'Avesnes-sur-Helpe', 'Mons'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) Start: ±880 (infobox) against the 870 Meerssen mention; the early extent. (2) 1432 (infobox, Hainaut text) against 1433 (succession table; Jacqueline infobox 12 April 1433; Easter 1433 treaty of The Hague) against 1436 (Jacqueline's death, when the page says Philip 'inherited Hainaut and Holland'). (3) The Wittelsbach succession (Louis IV's wife Margaret, 1345) is not on this page; the 1356 rename is the page's union date. (4) The 1051/1067/1071 sequence: the page has Baldwin VI ruling both from 1067 and the union ending 1071; 'the unification of Hainaut as an Imperial fief' after Arnulf's defeat in 1071. (5) Treaty dates of 1659 and 1679 (the page says 1679 for Nijmegen, 1797 for the northern cession against 1795 annexation). (6) Humphrey of Gloucester's recognition in December 1424 is an episode of the Jacqueline conflict and is not entered as a territorial event.
